title: TEMPO
body: Tempo takes its name from musical time, which suits a performing arts venue. That rhythm is set by the repeating wooden members forming the sculpture. The word shares a root with temporal and temporary, and both apply to the site.

The meadow is surrounded by the built environment but reads as separate from it. The skyline beyond asserts permanence, while the meadow, almost entirely unbuilt, would return to its natural state within months if left alone. That is not fragility but a different kind of resilience.

Architecture usually treats the temporary as a shortcoming. Here it is the premise. Materials and interventions were chosen to leave as little trace on the meadow as possible while making the strongest impression on those who visit. The amphitheater works as a venue, but its purpose is to establish a temporal and spatial connection to the site.
